item.title: Statement by Premier Rob Lantz on Mi’kmaw History Month
item.description:
Statement by Premier Rob Lantz on Mi’kmaw History Month jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/05/2026 - 13:49

Premier of Prince Edward Island, Rob Lantz issued the following statement:

“October marks Mi’kmaw History Month, a time to learn more about the history, culture, language and traditions of the Mi’kmaq people.

The Mi’kmaq people have been part of the history of Prince Edward Island for thousands of years, and their contributions continue to be an important part of the province today. Learning more about that history, including the experiences of Mi’kmaq people, is an important part of reconciliation.

Throughout October, the Indigenous Relations Secretariat will offer a series of lunch-and-learn sessions led by Mi’kmaq presenters for public service employees. KAIROS Blanket Exercises will also be offered by the Lennox Island Mi’kmaq Cultural Centre, giving employees additional opportunities to learn more about Mi’kmaq history, culture and perspectives.

I encourage all Islanders to take part in Mi’kmaw History Month, by exploring the stories, traditions and cultures of the Mi’kmaq people, and to carry those lessons forward throughout the year.” 

Learn more about Mi’kmaw History Month.

item.title: Nominations open for 2027 Heritage Awards
item.description:
Nominations open for 2027 Heritage Awards jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/05/2026 - 10:39

Island residents are invited to submit nominations for the 2027 Heritage Awards.

Each year, the PEI Museum and Heritage Foundation presents Heritage Awards from a variety of categories to Island residents who work to protect, share, and promote our history. The awards recognize volunteers, community groups, and individuals who make an impact through meaningful activities, research, storytelling, and more.

" The stories, traditions, and historic places that define Prince Edward Island are preserved through the dedication of people in communities across the province. The Heritage Awards are an opportunity to recognize and celebrate those who help keep our Island's history alive and ensure it can be shared with future generations."

- Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson

“The Island’s story is preserved and shared by so many incredible people who spend their time and energy keeping our history alive. The annual Heritage Awards are our chance to celebrate these amazing individuals and groups. If you know someone in your community who is making a difference, we’d love to see their name put forward.”

- PEI Museum and Heritage Foundation executive director Matthew McRae

Nominations are open until November 27, 2026.  Nominations can be submitted through the PEI Museum Heritage website or by calling 902-368-6600.

For more information visit: PEI Museum Heritage Awards

item.title: PEI 2025-2026 Public Accounts show improvement in deficit, increased revenues
item.description:
PEI 2025-2026 Public Accounts show improvement in deficit, increased revenues jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 16:04

Today, the Government of PEI released all three volumes of the 2025-2026 Public Accounts showing its audited financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026.

The 2025-2026 fiscal year ended with a deficit of $355.5 million. This was $94.1 million lower than forecast in spring 2026, as part of the operating budget estimates. 

“Islanders expect us to manage the finances responsibly and these Public Accounts demonstrate that we are taking action on responsible fiscal management. Our strong economy has helped increase revenues, and we’re within our target fiscal anchors. We’re positioning our province for sustainable future growth while continuing to invest in what matters most to Islanders.”

- Minister of Finance and Affordability Jill Burridge

Revenues for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, were just over $3.3 billion. This is $192.7 million higher than in 2024-25 and $45.5 million above the 2026 spring forecast. The increase from spring 2026 forecast was mainly due to higher than anticipated provincial corporate tax revenue.

Expenditures for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, were just over $3.6 billion. Key areas of expenditure include:

  • $1.4 billion in Health and Wellness and Health PEI
  • $475.2 million in Education and Early Years
  • $232.0 million in Social Development and Seniors
  • $223.1 million in Transportation and Infrastructure
  • $200.8 million in Workforce, Advanced Learning and Population

Net debt at March 31, 2026, was $3.7 billion, or 32.3 per cent of GDP, reflecting strong ongoing investments in tangible capital assets. 

Public Accounts is an annual financial summary and accountability report of the Government of Prince Edward Island, audited by the Auditor General. 

For more information on public accounts, visit Public Accounts | Government of Prince Edward Island.

item.title: Older adults recognized with Senior Islander of the Year Award
item.description:
Older adults recognized with Senior Islander of the Year Award jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/02/2026 - 15:01

Nine Islanders were honoured today with the 2026 Senior Islander of the Year Award for their lasting impact on communities across Prince Edward Island.

The award promotes positive images of aging and celebrates the many contributions of PEI residents who are 65 years and older. This year’s and past recipients have been recognized for a variety of efforts, including community activities and engagement, volunteering, fundraising, education, research, fitness and recreation. 

“Congratulations to all the winners of the 2026 Senior Islander of the Year award. Receiving this award is a significant honour. Your dedication, compassion, and community spirit have touched the lives of many Islanders. We are grateful for your contributions and proud to celebrate your accomplishments.”

- Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

The winners of the 2026 award are:

  • Carol White (Murray Harbour) 
  • Hu Meihua (Stratford) 
  • Kaye Morrison (Charlottetown)
  • Miriam Lank (Meadowbank) 
  • Georgie Smith (Kinkora)
  • Carol MacLean (Summerside)
  • Doug Bryson (Union Corner) 
  • Claude Blaquière (Mont-Carmel)
  • Beverley Ann Boulter (O’Leary)

“The older adults we are recognizing today have demonstrated an exceptional commitment to their communities,” said chair of the PEI Seniors’ Secretariat Peter Holman. “Through their leadership, generosity, and dedication, they have created lasting positive change and strengthened the communities they serve. It is a privilege to celebrate and recognize their achievements, and to thank them for making our province a better place.”

To learn more, visit Senior Islander of the Year Award.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
